questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Recede
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"recede"** means to move back or withdraw; to become more distant. (पीछे हटना)

 
 
• **Example: **The floodwaters began to recede after the heavy rains stopped.
 
 
 
• **"Extend" **refers to stretching out or spreading something to a greater extent or over a wider area. (फैलाना)
 
 
• **Example: **They decided to extend the road to connect the new housing development to the city.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'recede' **is **'extend'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Ebb **(घटना): The movement of the tide out to sea; to decline or diminish.

 
 
• **Example:** The enthusiasm of the crowd began to ebb as the event dragged on.
 
 
 
• **Fade **(मंद पड़ना): To gradually become less distinct or lose brightness.
 
 
• **Example: **The colors of the painting started to fade after years of exposure to sunlight.
 
 
 
• **Wane** (क्षीण होना): To decrease in size, extent, or degree.
 
 
• **Example:** His influence in the company began to wane after the new management took over.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in ****Indirect****/Direct speech.**

My father said to the stranger, "Where do you live?"

options.text: My father asked the stranger where he lives.
My father asked the stranger where he has been living.
My father asked where he lives to the stranger.
My father asked the stranger where he lived.

questions.solution:
Ans: My father asked the stranger where he lived.

Sol: Sentence 1 uses the incorrect tense (present) in reported speech, Sentence 2 also uses an incorrect tense (past continuous) and Sentence 3 changes the structure of the sentence unnecessarily. Only Sentence 4 changes the first person to third person and present tense to past tense. Hence, Sentence 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

The shoes were very expensive; I couldn't afford (to buying) them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**to buy**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 If you can afford something, you have enough money to be able to pay for it. This word usually follows ‘can’, ‘could’, or ‘be able to’
 
 
• 
 Afford is never followed by a verb in the -ing form. Use an infinitive:

 
 
• 
 ✗ What about people who cannot afford going to these kind of centres?
 
 
• 
 ✓ What about people who cannot afford to go to these kind of centres?
 
 
• 
 ✗ We can afford buying 10 new computers this year.
 
 
• 
 ✓ We can afford to buy 10 new computers this year.
 
 
 

​**Thus, the correct sentence is: ***The shoes were very expensive; I couldn't afford **to buy**__ them.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

After they (had finished) eating they went for a walk.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**no improvement**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• When two actions of the past are given, then **the action that happened first should be in past perfect tense** and the second should be in past indefinite tense.
 
• **Example:**

 
 

 **Event A**
 **Event B**
 
 

 John had gone out
 when I arrived in the office.
 
 

 **Event A**
 **Event B**
 
 

 I had saved my document
 before the computer crashed.
 
 

 **Event B**
 **Event A**
 
 

 When they arrived
 we had already started cooking.
 
 

 
• Here 'finishing eating' is the first action and 'going for a walk' is the second action.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

My sister had a tough time (1)/removing the chewing gum that (2)/stuck with her hair.(3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Ans: 3

Sol: ‘Stuck with something’ means intertwined with something while ‘stuck to something’ means attached to something. In the given sentence, ‘stuck to’ is a better fit since the chewing gum cannot be intertwined in her hair, but rather attached to her hair. Hence, the correct sentence is: ‘My sister had a tough time removing the chewing gum that stuck to her hair.”

questions.question:

**The room which yielded so**

X-the fourth floor of a

Y-boarding-house in Bleecker Street

Z-much satisfaction to the two boys was on

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.**

Not being what it purports to be
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. Spurious.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Spurious"** means something that is not being what it purports to be; false or fake. (कृत्रिम, झूठा)

 
 
• **Example: **The document was found to be spurious, and the transaction was declared invalid.
 
 
 
• **"Legitimate" **refers to something that is conforming to the law or to rules; genuine. (वैध)
 
 
• **Example: **He presented a legitimate argument to support his case.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. Spurious.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Legitimate **(वैध): Conforming to the law or to rules; genuine.

 
 
• **Example:** He presented a legitimate argument to support his case.
 
 
 
• **Palpable **(स्पष्ट): Something that is clear and easily perceived; it could refer to an atmosphere so intense as to seem almost tangible.
 
 
• **Example: **The excitement in the room was palpable as we awaited the announcement of the winners.
 
 
 
• **Evident** (स्पष्ट): Plain or obvious; clearly seen or understood.
 
 
• **Example:** His happiness was evident from the broad smile on his face.
